cards.title: Imports and aliases
cards.explanation: Brings collection and I/O types into scope. The grouped import includes the io module itself, and 'as' gives fmt::Result a distinct local name.

cards.title: Function definitions
cards.explanation: Defines a function that returns the square of an integer through its final expression, and a greeting function that borrows a string slice and returns ().

cards.title: Modules and visibility
cards.explanation: Declares private and public modules, limits internal() to this crate, exposes public(), and re-exports api::Client at this module's path.

cards.title: Constants and statics
cards.code:
const MAX_RETRIES: usize = 3;
static APP_NAME: &str = "demo";
cards.explanation: Defines a compile-time constant for the retry limit and an immutable static string reference with a fixed storage location for the program's lifetime.

cards.title: Bindings and shadowing
cards.explanation: Shadows count with a new binding whose value is one larger. A separate mutable binding allows total to be updated in place.

cards.title: Ownership and moving
cards.explanation: Transfers ownership of the String from original to moved, then into consume(). Each previous binding becomes unavailable after the move; consume returns the byte length.

cards.title: Shared borrowing
keywords: reference read lend no move shared
cards.explanation: Passes a shared reference to the String as a string slice to read its byte length. Ownership stays with text, so it can still be printed afterward.

cards.title: Mutable borrowing
cards.explanation: Passes an exclusive mutable reference to append(), which adds an exclamation mark to the existing String without taking ownership.

cards.title: Clone and Copy
cards.explanation: Cloning a String makes an independent owned copy. Assigning an i32 copies its value automatically, so both integer bindings remain usable.

cards.title: String and str
keywords: text owned borrowed as_str to_owned format
cards.explanation: Creates an owned, growable String from a borrowed string slice, appends text, borrows a view of the result, and formats it into a new String.

cards.title: Arrays and slices
cards.explanation: Creates a fixed four-element array, borrows the whole array or just indices 1 and 2 as slices, and retrieves the first element as an Option without indexing panics.

cards.title: Handle an optional value
keywords: missing absence nullable maybe some none
cards.explanation: Unwraps Some(42) with a match, using 0 when the value is None. Both cases produce the integer assigned to number.

cards.title: Transform and default Option
keywords: map and_then unwrap_or fallback default chain
cards.explanation: Parses optional text into an integer, turns parsing failures into None, doubles a successful value, and uses 0 if no value remains. This example produces 84.

cards.title: Borrow or take Option contents
cards.explanation: Reads and modifies the String inside an Option through borrowed references. take() then moves the String out and leaves name as None.

cards.title: Handle a fallible result
keywords: error success failure recover ok err
cards.explanation: Parses text as an integer and handles both outcomes explicitly: the number goes to standard output, while a parsing error goes to standard error.

cards.title: Propagate errors with question mark
keywords: propagate error early return question mark
cards.explanation: Reads a file and parses its trimmed contents as an integer. Each '?' returns early on failure, converting the error into the function's boxed error type.

cards.title: Transform Result and errors
cards.code:
let result: Result<i32, String> = "42"
    .parse::<i32>()
    .map(|n| n * 2)
    .map_err(|error| error.to_string());
cards.explanation: Doubles a successfully parsed integer and converts a parsing error into a String. map changes the success value; map_err changes only the error.

cards.title: Match patterns and guards
keywords: match exhaustive switch guard range or wildcard
cards.code:
match value {
    0 => "zero",
    1 | 2 => "small",
    3..=9 => "single digit",
    n if n < 0 => "negative",
    _ => "other",
}
cards.explanation: Classifies a value using exact values, alternatives, an inclusive range, and a conditional guard. The wildcard arm handles all remaining cases.

cards.title: Conditional pattern binding
keywords: if let while let some destructure
cards.explanation: Runs the first block only when the optional value is Some. The while-let loop repeatedly pops and processes stack items until pop() returns None.

cards.title: Early exit with let else
keywords: let else early return missing destructure
cards.explanation: Extracts the number from Some or exits the function immediately on None. After the let-else statement, number is available for printing.

cards.title: Struct definition and update
cards.explanation: Defines a Point with named fields. Struct update syntax sets the new x value and takes the remaining y field from origin.

cards.title: Enum variants with data
keywords: tagged union variant tuple record sum type
cards.explanation: Defines variants carrying no data, a String, or named coordinates. Matching selects the variant and extracts its data for the corresponding action.

cards.title: Methods and associated functions
keywords: impl self constructor method associated new
cards.explanation: Adds an associated constructor called with Point::new(), and a method that borrows a Point to calculate its distance from the origin.

cards.title: Trait and implementation
keywords: interface shared behavior contract default method
cards.explanation: Defines a shared area() interface and implements it for Circle using its radius. The method borrows the circle rather than consuming it.

cards.title: Generics and trait bounds
keywords: generic type parameter where bound display
cards.explanation: Restricts generic types to the operations each function needs: Display for printing and Clone for creating an owned duplicate from a reference.

cards.title: Associated types
keywords: associated type self item trait iterator
cards.explanation: Lets each Source implementation choose its Item type. Counter chooses u32 and increments its stored value whenever next() is called.

cards.title: Trait objects
cards.explanation: Calls Draw methods through trait objects using runtime dispatch. Boxes can own different concrete drawing types, while &dyn Draw borrows one.

cards.title: Reference lifetime parameters
keywords: outlive reference validity dangling lifetime a
cards.explanation: Returns whichever input string has the greater byte length. The shared lifetime parameter ensures the returned borrow cannot outlive either input borrow.

cards.title: Borrowed fields and lifetimes
cards.explanation: Stores a borrowed string slice in Excerpt. The lifetime parameter keeps the excerpt from outliving its source text; text() returns a borrowed view.

cards.title: Iterator map filter collect
keywords: transform collection filter pipeline each element
cards.code:
let values = vec![1, 2, 3, 4];
let doubled: Vec<i32> = values
    .iter()
    .copied()
    .filter(|n| n % 2 == 0)
    .map(|n| n * 2)
    .collect();
cards.explanation: Borrows the vector, copies its integers, keeps the even ones, doubles them, and collects a new vector containing [4, 8].

cards.title: Borrow mutate or consume iterators
cards.explanation: Shows three iteration modes: iter() shares references, iter_mut() permits in-place changes, and into_iter() consumes the collection and yields owned elements.

cards.title: Iterator fold enumerate and zip
keywords: reduce accumulator sum index pair zip
cards.explanation: Accumulates a sum with fold(), pairs each value with its index using enumerate(), and zips names with scores until either sequence ends.

cards.title: Closures and move captures
cards.explanation: Defines and calls an addition closure. The move closure owns the captured String and returns its byte length when called.

cards.title: Growable vectors of borrowed and owned strings
cards.explanation: Creates growable vectors of borrowed string slices and owned Strings, then appends one value to each. Vec lengths can change at runtime; borrowed strings must remain valid while their references are used.

cards.title: Vectors and safe access
keywords: list dynamic array push get pop
cards.explanation: Creates a growable vector and appends an element. get() safely returns an optional reference, and pop() removes the last element as an Option.

cards.title: HashMap and entry
keywords: dictionary key value lookup insert entry count
cards.explanation: Counts repeated words in a HashMap. entry().or_insert(0) supplies a mutable counter for each word; get() borrows the final count for 'rust'.

cards.title: Loops ranges and break values
keywords: for while loop range repeat break continue
cards.explanation: Iterates over 0, 1, and 2 using an exclusive range. The loop expression then breaks on the third attempt and yields 6 as its result.

cards.title: Async functions and await
cards.explanation: Defines an async function and awaits its result, propagating any error. It also creates and awaits a separate async block; futures progress when polled by an executor.

cards.title: Unit tests and assertions
cards.explanation: Compiles the module only for tests, imports its parent's items, and checks a sum and a positive-value predicate in a test function.

cards.title: Derive standard traits
keywords: derive debug clone partialeq eq default
cards.explanation: Generates standard trait implementations for User. default() supplies empty and false field values, and Debug enables the debug-format print.

cards.title: Box and recursive types
cards.explanation: Uses Box to give the recursive List enum a finite size. Each Node owns its next list through a heap allocation.

cards.title: Reference counted shared ownership
keywords: rc arc shared ownership reference counting thread
cards.explanation: Creates shared ownership with Rc for local use and Arc for use across threads. Cloning either pointer increases the reference count rather than duplicating its contents.

cards.title: Interior mutability and locks
keywords: refcell mutex borrow_mut lock shared mutable
cards.explanation: Mutates a vector through RefCell's runtime borrow checks and increments a value protected by Mutex. The lock guard releases the lock when dropped.

cards.title: From Into TryFrom and parse
keywords: convert parse into from try_from fallible
cards.explanation: Uses Into and From for infallible conversions, and parse() and TryFrom for conversions that can fail. '?' propagates conversion errors.

cards.title: Destructure structs and tuples
keywords: destructure tuple fields rename rest ref
cards.explanation: Extracts tuple and struct fields, renames some bindings, and ignores remaining fields with '..'. Matching &message borrows its text instead of moving it.

cards.title: Numeric literal forms
cards.explanation: Writes numbers in decimal, binary, octal, hexadecimal, and floating-point forms. Underscores improve readability, while suffixes choose the numeric type.

cards.title: Numeric casts and checked conversion
cards.explanation: Widens a u8 without loss, attempts a checked narrowing that fails for 300, and casts 3.8 to an integer by truncating its fractional part to produce 3.

cards.title: Checked saturating and wrapping arithmetic
cards.explanation: Shows overflow policies: checked_add returns None, saturating_add stays at 255, and wrapping_add produces 0. Checked division by zero also returns None.

cards.title: Tuple construction and access
cards.explanation: Creates a tuple of different types, reads fields by numeric index, and destructures it into bindings. A trailing comma distinguishes a one-element tuple.

cards.title: Arrays of borrowed and owned strings
cards.explanation: Declares fixed-size arrays of borrowed string slices and owned Strings, then borrows the first array as a slice. Array lengths are part of their types; use a Vec when the number of strings needs to change.

cards.title: Fixed arrays and from_fn
cards.explanation: Initializes an array with a repeated value, then uses from_fn to compute each element from its index, including independently allocated Strings.

cards.title: If expressions produce values
cards.explanation: Uses an if/else chain as an expression. The branch selected by score produces the string assigned to label.

cards.title: Range syntax and containment
cards.explanation: Contrasts exclusive and inclusive range ends, checks whether score lies between 0 and 100, and iterates over 4 down to 0.

cards.title: Absolute relative and parent module paths
cards.explanation: Imports items relative to the crate root, current module, and parent module. pub use also makes Client available through this module's public path.

cards.title: Type aliases
cards.explanation: Names existing types for readability, including a generic Result and a function pointer. Aliases do not create distinct new types.

cards.title: Tuple and unit structs
cards.explanation: Defines distinct wrapper and coordinate types with unnamed fields, plus a fieldless marker type. Destructuring UserId extracts its inner integer.

cards.title: Unicode characters versus bytes
cards.explanation: Counts UTF-8 bytes separately from Unicode scalar values: 'café' has 5 bytes and 4 chars. char_indices() reports byte offsets, not character positions.

cards.title: Split whitespace delimiters and lines
cards.explanation: Splits text into whitespace-separated words, comma-delimited fields, and lines. split_once() returns the two sides of the first '=' as an Option.

cards.title: Trim and strip string boundaries
cards.explanation: Borrows text with surrounding whitespace or leading zeroes removed. strip_prefix() and strip_suffix() return None if the requested boundary text is absent.

cards.title: Build a string with formatted writes
cards.explanation: Appends formatted text directly to an existing String. writeln! also adds a newline, and the score is formatted to two decimal places.

cards.title: Raw string and byte string literals
cards.explanation: Writes strings whose backslashes need no escaping, using '#' delimiters when quotes occur inside. Byte strings produce byte slices rather than str values.

cards.title: Replace and join text
cards.explanation: Creates new strings by replacing all matches or only the first comma, joining pieces with a separator, and applying Unicode lowercase conversion.

cards.title: UTF-8 boundary aware string slicing
cards.explanation: Uses byte ranges with get() to avoid panics on invalid UTF-8 boundaries. For 'café', offset 4 splits 'é', so get(..4) returns None.

cards.title: UTF-8 conversion from bytes
cards.explanation: Validates bytes as borrowed or owned UTF-8 text. The lossy conversion replaces invalid sequences with the replacement character instead of returning an error.

cards.title: Character classification and conversion
cards.explanation: Converts a decimal digit to a number, classifies letters and whitespace, and attempts to turn a Unicode code point into a char.

cards.title: Reborrow a mutable reference
cards.explanation: Temporarily reborrows a mutable reference for a function call and then as a shared string view. Once the shared borrow ends, the original reference can mutate again.

cards.title: Move out with take and replace
cards.explanation: Moves values out through a mutable reference while leaving a valid replacement. take() leaves an empty String; replace() installs 'new' and returns the previous value.

cards.title: Reuse an allocation with clone_from
cards.explanation: Copies the source String into an existing target. clone_from() can reuse the target's allocated capacity instead of creating a fresh destination allocation.

cards.title: Clone on write with Cow
cards.explanation: Starts with borrowed text in Cow. to_mut() creates an owned copy when mutation is needed, and into_owned() then returns that owned String.

cards.title: Weak references and upgrading
cards.explanation: Creates a non-owning Weak reference to an Rc value. upgrade() returns shared ownership only if the value still has a strong owner, helping avoid ownership cycles.

cards.title: Resource cleanup with Drop
cards.explanation: Defines cleanup that runs when a Session is dropped, printing a message as the value leaves scope or is explicitly dropped.

cards.title: Turn absence into an error
cards.explanation: Converts None into an error and propagates it with '?'. ok_or_else() constructs its error lazily only when the optional name is missing.

cards.title: Transpose an optional fallible value
cards.explanation: Parses optional text and swaps Option<Result<T, E>> into Result<Option<T>, E>. Missing text stays Ok(None), while parsing errors become Err.

cards.title: Flatten nested Option values
cards.explanation: Removes one layer of Option nesting. Some(Some(42)) becomes Some(42), while Some(None) becomes None.

cards.title: Combine two optional values
cards.explanation: Combines a name and age into Some((name, age)) only when both are present. If either input is None, the combined value is None.

cards.title: Keep an optional value only when it matches
cards.explanation: Keeps an optional number only when its predicate succeeds. A missing value or a failed predicate produces None.

cards.title: Insert or initialize an optional value
cards.explanation: Lazily initializes a missing name and returns a mutable reference for editing it. insert() then replaces any existing name and returns a reference to the replacement.

cards.title: Borrow the dereferenced Option contents
cards.explanation: Borrows an optional String as an optional str slice. The mutable form permits in-place ASCII uppercasing without taking the String out of the Option.

cards.title: Check optional contents with predicates
cards.explanation: Checks whether an Option is present or absent, and whether its contained number satisfies a predicate. is_some_and() returns false for None.

cards.title: Chain fallible operations
cards.explanation: Doubles a successfully parsed u8 using a wider integer, then performs another fallible parse. and_then() keeps a single Result layer and forwards any error.

cards.title: Transpose a fallible optional value
cards.code:
let result: Result<Option<i32>, &str> = Ok(Some(42));
let optional: Option<Result<i32, &str>> = result.transpose();
cards.explanation: Swaps Result<Option<T>, E> into Option<Result<T, E>>. Ok(None) becomes None, while an error becomes Some(Err(error)).

cards.title: Observe results without consuming contents
cards.explanation: Logs either a successful number or its parsing error through borrowed references, while passing the original Result onward unchanged.

cards.title: Borrow success or error values
cards.explanation: Borrows both sides of a Result, then extracts an optional reference to either the success value or the error without moving the original Strings.

cards.title: Custom error with Display and Error
cards.explanation: Defines an error type with Debug, a human-readable Display message, and the standard Error trait so it can participate in normal error handling.

cards.title: Match slices with rest patterns
cards.explanation: Matches empty, single-element, and longer slices. The rest pattern binds the middle slice while separately borrowing the first and last elements.

cards.title: Bind a value while matching a pattern
cards.explanation: Uses '@' to retain the matched value while checking a range pattern. Each arm prints the value with its matching category.

cards.title: Borrow with ref and ref mut patterns
cards.explanation: Borrows the String inside Some using ref, then borrows it mutably using ref mut to append a character. Neither pattern moves the String out.

cards.title: Match tuples and ignore fields
cards.explanation: Matches both coordinates together to recognize the origin and axes. Patterns bind the nonzero coordinate; the wildcard handles other points.

cards.title: Test a pattern with matches
cards.explanation: Produces booleans from pattern matches, including an ASCII digit range, a guarded positive Option, and an empty slice pattern.

cards.title: Filter and transform in one step
cards.code:
let numbers: Vec<i32> = ["1", "bad", "3"]
    .into_iter()
    .filter_map(|text| text.parse().ok())
    .collect();
cards.explanation: Parses each string and discards failed parses using filter_map(). The collected vector contains [1, 3].

cards.title: Flatten transformed sequences
cards.explanation: Splits each line into words and combines all those word iterators into one sequence. flatten() similarly removes a single layer of nested collections.

cards.title: Find an element or its position
cards.explanation: Finds the first value over 10, its position, or the first successfully parsed integer. These operations stop at the first match and return an Option.

cards.title: Check whether any or all elements match
cards.code:
let has_negative = values.iter().any(|n| *n < 0);
let all_positive = values.iter().all(|n| *n > 0);
cards.explanation: Tests whether at least one value is negative and whether every value is positive. Both operations stop as soon as their answer is known.

cards.title: Limit and skip iterator elements
cards.explanation: Selects a five-element page after skipping ten items, takes an initial positive run, and skips only the leading zeroes before yielding the rest.

cards.title: Chain sequences and append one item
cards.explanation: Consumes two sequences consecutively, appends one extra value, and collects all their elements into a single vector.

cards.title: Repeat an iterator with a limit
cards.explanation: Builds finite collections from repeating iterators by limiting them with take(). repeat_with() constructs a fresh String for each yielded item.

cards.title: Peek at the next iterator item
cards.explanation: Reads characters while looking ahead without consuming the next one. If the next character is ':', an extra next() consumes it before printing the current character.

cards.title: Carry state through an iterator
cards.explanation: Maintains running state while iterating. Each number updates the accumulated sum, producing a vector of running totals [1, 3, 6].

cards.title: Stop a fold at the first failure
cards.explanation: Parses and sums text values, stopping at the first error. Because 'bad' cannot be parsed, the final result is an Err rather than a partial sum.

cards.title: Collect results and stop at the first error
cards.code:
let numbers: Result<Vec<i32>, _> = ["1", "2", "bad"]
    .into_iter()
    .map(str::parse::<i32>)
    .collect();
cards.explanation: Collects successful parses into a vector only if every parse succeeds. The first failure stops collection and becomes the overall Result's error.

cards.title: Split pairs into separate collections
cards.code:
let pairs = [("Ada", 36), ("Grace", 85)];
let (names, ages): (Vec<_>, Vec<_>) = pairs.into_iter().unzip();
cards.explanation: Separates a sequence of name-age pairs into two vectors, preserving the pair order in each output.

cards.title: Collect pairs into a map
cards.explanation: Transforms each name into a key-value pair containing its byte length, then collects those pairs into a HashMap.

cards.title: Sum and multiply iterator values
cards.explanation: Calculates a sequence's sum and product, and reduces copied values to their maximum. reduce() returns None when there are no elements.

cards.title: Vector length and capacity
cards.explanation: Preallocates room for at least sixteen elements and extends the vector. reserve() ensures spare capacity; len() counts elements while capacity() reports available storage.

cards.title: Retain and deduplicate vector elements
cards.explanation: Removes nonpositive values, then doubles remaining values and keeps those below 100. Sorting before dedup() makes all equal values adjacent so duplicates are removed.

cards.title: Remove a vector range with drain
cards.explanation: Removes and collects values at indices 1 and 2, pops the final element, then truncates the remaining vector to one element.

cards.title: Split and append vectors
cards.explanation: Splits off the vector's tail at index 2, appends that tail back while emptying it, and extends the original vector with two more values.

cards.title: Update existing entries or insert defaults
cards.explanation: Increments an existing word counter or inserts 1 for a missing key. The second entry operation initializes a missing vector only when needed and returns a mutable reference.

cards.title: Borrow mutate and remove map values
cards.explanation: Borrows a score mutably for an update, checks key membership, and removes entries. remove() returns the value; remove_entry() returns the key-value pair.

cards.title: Set membership and set operations
cards.explanation: Builds two sets and collects their shared values, combined values, and values unique to the first set. HashSet iteration order is unspecified.

cards.title: Ordered map range queries
cards.explanation: Uses an ordered map to visit keys 1 through 2 in sorted order and retrieve the smallest key-value pair without removing it.

cards.title: Sorted unique values
cards.explanation: Stores unique values in sorted order, inserts 4, removes the smallest value, and iterates over the remaining values in ascending order.

cards.title: Double ended queue operations
cards.explanation: Adds ordinary work at the back of a double-ended queue and urgent work at the front. pop_front() retrieves the urgent item first.

cards.title: Maximum and minimum priority queues
cards.explanation: Retrieves the largest value from a default BinaryHeap. Wrapping values in Reverse changes priority so the second heap retrieves the smallest value first.

cards.title: Sort by key or custom comparison
cards.explanation: Sorts values in ascending order, users by age or name, and values in descending order using Reverse as the sort key.

cards.title: Sort floats with total_cmp
cards.explanation: Sorts floating-point values using a total order that includes NaN and signed zero, and compares two floats with the same ordering method.

cards.title: Binary search a sorted slice
cards.explanation: Searches an already sorted vector. If 4 is absent, the error contains the insertion position needed to add it while preserving sort order.

cards.title: Sliding windows and disjoint chunks
cards.explanation: Visits overlapping two-element windows and separate three-element chunks. chunks_exact() yields only full chunks and exposes leftover elements through remainder().

cards.title: Borrow disjoint mutable slices
cards.explanation: Splits an array into two non-overlapping mutable slices at index 2. Each slice can then be changed independently without conflicting mutable borrows.

cards.title: Fill reverse and rotate slices
cards.explanation: Updates a slice in place by filling it, reversing its order, and rotating elements with wraparound. Its length stays the same.

cards.title: Implement Display for a newtype
cards.explanation: Defines how a UserId prints through Display, formatting the wrapped number with a 'user-' prefix.

cards.title: Implement an infallible conversion
cards.explanation: Implements a lossless conversion from u64 to the UserId wrapper. Implementing From also makes the corresponding into() conversion available.

cards.title: Implement a fallible conversion
cards.explanation: Constructs Positive only for integers greater than zero. Invalid values return a string error through TryFrom's associated Error type.

cards.title: Parse a custom type with FromStr
cards.explanation: Makes UserId parseable from text. Integer parsing errors are forwarded, while a successful number is wrapped in UserId.

cards.title: Implement Deref for a wrapper
cards.explanation: Lets a Name wrapper provide a shared str view of its inner String through Deref, enabling dereference coercions and string-slice methods.

cards.title: Implement addition for a newtype
cards.explanation: Defines the '+' operator for two Distance values. Addition consumes both wrappers and returns a new Distance containing their summed numbers.

cards.title: Implement Default for configuration
cards.explanation: Provides a standard default configuration with three retries, available through Config::default().

cards.title: Trait associated constants
cards.explanation: Declares a constant as part of a trait's interface. Buffer supplies its own MAX value of 1024 in the implementation.

cards.title: Higher ranked lifetime bounds
cards.explanation: Requires a callback that can accept a string borrow of any lifetime and return a borrow with that same lifetime, allowing it to work with the local String.

cards.title: Return an opaque iterator
cards.explanation: Returns an iterator over even numbers below limit while hiding its concrete type. In an argument, impl Display accepts any type that supports that trait.

cards.title: Const generic array lengths
cards.explanation: Uses a compile-time length parameter to support arrays of different sizes in a sum function and a fixed-size byte buffer type.

cards.title: Declarative expression macro
cards.explanation: Defines a macro that evaluates its input expression once, stores the result, and adds it to itself. twice!(21) produces 42.

cards.title: Macro repetition and optional trailing comma
cards.explanation: Accepts zero or more comma-separated expressions with an optional trailing comma and expands them into a vec! invocation.

cards.title: Feature gated compilation
cards.explanation: Compiles one of two log functions according to the logging feature: one prints to standard error and the other ignores its argument.

cards.title: Platform specific compilation
cards.explanation: Selects platform-specific function definitions at compile time. cfg! separately produces a boolean indicating whether the target operating system is Linux.

cards.title: Test expected panics
cards.explanation: Passes only if the test panics with a message containing 'invalid input', verifying the expected failure behavior.

cards.title: Tests returning Result
cards.explanation: Allows a test to use '?' by returning Result. A parsing error fails the test; successful parsing is checked before returning Ok(()).

cards.title: Formatting width precision and radix
cards.explanation: Formats values with zero padding, right alignment, decimal precision, hexadecimal and binary notation, and pretty Debug output.

cards.title: Read and write whole files
cards.explanation: Reads whole files as UTF-8 text or raw bytes, creates an output directory and any missing parents, and writes the text to an output file.

cards.title: Read a file line by line
cards.explanation: Wraps a file in a buffered reader and processes one line at a time without loading the whole file. '?' forwards file-opening and line-reading errors.

cards.title: Buffered file output
cards.explanation: Buffers writes to a newly created file, writes formatted and raw byte lines, and explicitly flushes so any final write error can be handled.

cards.title: Build and inspect paths
cards.explanation: Builds a path using native path operations, borrows its filename, extension, and parent, and creates a separate path with a changed extension.

cards.title: Inspect path components without string splitting
cards.explanation: Examines structural path components, distinguishing ordinary names from '..'. This inspects the path without accessing files or resolving it to an absolute path.

cards.title: Command line arguments and environment
cards.explanation: Reads command-line arguments while skipping the program name and looks up HOME. The OS-string variants preserve values that are not valid Unicode.

cards.title: Read a line from standard input
cards.explanation: Reads a line into a String, borrows a view with trailing whitespace removed, and prints the resulting input.

cards.title: Spawn and join a thread
cards.explanation: Moves a vector into a worker thread, computes its sum there, and waits for the result with join(). A worker panic triggers expect().

cards.title: Scoped threads can borrow local data
cards.explanation: Starts a scoped worker that borrows the local array. The scope ensures all its threads finish before their borrowed local data can go out of scope.

cards.title: Send values through a channel
cards.explanation: Moves a String from a worker thread to the receiver through a channel. recv() waits for the message, and join() waits for the worker to finish.

cards.title: Bounded channel and nonblocking receive
cards.explanation: Creates a channel with room for two messages. try_recv() checks immediately and distinguishes a received value, an empty queue, and disconnection.

cards.title: Share mutable state between threads
cards.explanation: Shares a counter with a worker through Arc and protects mutation with Mutex. After joining the worker, the main thread locks and reads the updated counter.

cards.title: Atomic counter without a mutex
cards.explanation: Increments a counter atomically and reads it without a mutex. fetch_add() returns the previous value; Relaxed ordering does not synchronize other memory accesses.

cards.title: Initialize a shared value once
cards.explanation: Initializes a static String on the first call and returns a shared reference on later calls. OnceLock coordinates initialization safely across threads.

cards.title: Thread local mutable state
cards.explanation: Gives each thread its own Cell counter. with() accesses the current thread's value and increments it without sharing mutable state across threads.

cards.title: Return a future without async fn
cards.explanation: Returns an async block as an opaque Future from a regular function. Awaiting that future produces the integer 42.

cards.title: Move owned data into an async block
cards.explanation: Transfers ownership of a String into an async block. Awaiting the resulting future computes the String's byte length.

cards.title: Arithmetic comparison and compound assignment
cards.explanation: Shows arithmetic, comparisons, grouping, and assignment operators. Integer division truncates toward zero: 10 / 3 is 3 and 10 % 3 is 1. Parentheses override precedence; division by zero is invalid.

cards.title: Boolean negation and short circuit evaluation
cards.explanation: Uses ! for boolean negation, && for logical AND, and || for logical OR. The right side of && runs only if its left side is true; || evaluates its right side only if the left side is false. The final expression avoids division by zero.

cards.title: Bit masks shifts and bitwise assignment
cards.explanation: Combines and tests bit flags with | and &, clears bits with & and !, and toggles bits with ^. Shift operators move the bits left or right. Unlike boolean && and ||, & and | evaluate both operands.

cards.title: Block values tail expressions and semicolons
cards.explanation: A block returns its final expression when that expression has no semicolon, so answer is 42. A block ending in a statement yields the unit value (). Bindings declared inside a block are local to it.

cards.title: Early returns unit and the never type
cards.explanation: return exits the current function immediately; a tail expression supplies its ordinary result. () is the unit type and may be omitted as a function return type. ! marks a function that never returns normally. Negating i32::MIN cannot be represented as i32.

cards.title: While loops with break and continue
cards.explanation: Repeats while the condition is true. continue skips to the next condition check, while break exits the loop. This example prints 1, 3, and 5. Unlike loop, while cannot return a value through break.

cards.title: Break or continue an outer labelled loop
cards.explanation: A label selects which enclosing loop break or continue targets. continue rows advances the outer for loop; break search exits the outer loop expression with 4. Labels resemble lifetimes but name control flow targets.

cards.title: Exit a labelled block with a value
cards.explanation: A labelled block allows an early break that supplies its result without repeating execution. Here the block returns 0 for None and otherwise doubles the contained value. break must name the block label; continue cannot target a block.

cards.title: Chain pattern bindings and conditions
cards.explanation: Rust 1.88+ with edition 2024 allows let chains in if and while conditions. Each successful pattern introduces bindings for subsequent operands and the body. Evaluation stops at the first failed pattern or false condition; chains use && rather than ||.

cards.title: Pass and call a function pointer
cards.explanation: The fn argument type is a callable function pointer with a fixed signature. Functions and noncapturing, non-async closures can coerce to it. Closures that capture environment values require a closure trait such as Fn instead.

cards.title: Fn FnMut and FnOnce callback bounds
cards.explanation: Fn supports calls through a shared reference, FnMut permits mutation of captured state, and FnOnce permits consuming captures. Fn also implements FnMut and FnOnce. move determines how captures enter the closure; it does not by itself make the closure callable only once.

cards.title: Return a closure that owns captured data
cards.explanation: Returns an opaque closure type implementing Fn. move copies amount into the closure so the returned value does not borrow the function local. Repeated calls add the same captured amount.

cards.title: Async closures produce awaitable calls
cards.explanation: Rust 1.85+ supports async closures. This closure owns prefix and produces a future each time it is called; awaiting the calls produces item-1 and item-2. An async closure can lend its captures to the futures it returns.

cards.title: Const functions and inline const blocks
cards.explanation: const fn may be called during constant evaluation or at runtime. A constant initializer and an inline const block require compile-time evaluation. This example creates a 16-byte array and an inline constant value of 36.

cards.title: Generic structs enums and implementations
cards.explanation: Declares type parameters on data types and repeats the parameter declaration on impl. Pair defaults its type parameter to i32 when omitted in a type annotation, but inference can select another type. Either has independent types for its variants.

cards.title: Supertraits and default trait methods
cards.explanation: Describe requires implementers to also implement Display. Its method body provides a default implementation, so i32 can use an empty impl. An implementation may override the default method.

cards.title: Disambiguate trait methods with qualified paths
cards.explanation: Type::method selects the inherent method here, while <Type as Trait>::method explicitly selects the trait implementation. The same qualified syntax selects a trait associated type, such as Add::Output.

cards.title: Explicit generic arguments and inferred placeholders
cards.explanation: The ::<...> form supplies explicit generic arguments in expression paths. An underscore asks the compiler to infer that argument; Vec<_> becomes Vec<i32> here. A type annotation can also constrain inference without a turbofish.

cards.title: Use a reserved keyword as a raw identifier
cards.explanation: The r# prefix allows most keywords to be used as identifiers, including fields and function names. The prefix escapes the spelling; it is not part of the identifier name. crate, self, Self, and super cannot be raw identifiers.

cards.title: Unsafe functions require explicit unsafe operations
cards.explanation: Calling an unsafe function requires an unsafe block and fulfilling its safety contract. read requires an aligned, initialized, readable pointer to a live i32. Its body explicitly marks the dereference unsafe, as expected in edition 2024. The pointer here refers to a live local value.

cards.title: Create and dereference raw pointers
cards.explanation: Raw borrows create pointers without creating references; forming these pointers is safe. Dereferencing requires unsafe and valid alignment, initialization, lifetime, and access permissions. The two accesses here occur sequentially on a live local, producing 42.

cards.title: Union fields share storage
cards.explanation: Union fields occupy the same storage and have no enum-style variant tag. Writing a field is safe; reading one requires unsafe and a valid value for the selected field type. Both fields here permit every bit pattern, and the byte order is platform dependent. repr(C) requests C-compatible layout.

cards.title: Declare foreign functions and a C ABI function
cards.explanation: An unsafe extern block declares a function provided by a native library; calling abs requires satisfying the C contract, including avoiding the minimum signed integer. extern C on a definition selects the C calling convention. It does not itself export an unmangled symbol. The native library must provide abs when linked.

cards.title: Assign several existing bindings by destructuring
cards.explanation: Destructuring assignment updates existing mutable bindings without introducing new ones. The tuple assignment swaps left and right, while the array assignment stores the first and last elements and ignores the middle.

cards.title: Enum discriminants and representation
cards.explanation: Assigns explicit numeric discriminants to a fieldless enum and chooses u8 as its representation. Casting Ready yields 2. A representation attribute does not make arbitrary integers valid enum values.

cards.title: Accept unsized types through references
cards.explanation: Type parameters normally have an implicit Sized bound. ?Sized relaxes that requirement, allowing str and slice types, which are accessed here through references. The Debug bound still applies.

cards.title: Associated types parameterized by lifetimes
cards.explanation: A generic associated type lets each implementation choose a family of types indexed by a parameter. String chooses borrowed string slices indexed by lifetime. Self: a requires the implementing type to outlive the selected borrow lifetime; the returned view borrows self.

cards.title: Lifetime bounds and static string references
cards.explanation: The long: short bound requires the first lifetime to outlive the second, allowing the reference to be shortened. A string literal can supply a static reference valid for the entire program. A T: static bound instead describes references contained by T and does not require an owned T value to live forever.

cards.title: Inner and outer lint attributes
cards.explanation: An inner #! attribute applies to its enclosing module; an outer # attribute applies to the next item. deny makes the specified lint an error, allow suppresses a lint, and must_use asks callers to handle a function result. let _ explicitly discards this result.

cards.title: Start an Axum HTTP server
cards.explanation: Builds an Axum router with a GET /health endpoint returning 'healthy', binds a local TCP listener on port 8080, and serves HTTP requests asynchronously.

cards.title: Start an Actix Web HTTP server
cards.explanation: Starts an Actix Web server on localhost port 8080. The application factory registers a GET /health handler returning 'healthy'.

cards.title: Route HTTP methods with Axum
cards.explanation: Connects HTTP methods and paths to Axum handlers: GET and POST for the collection, and GET, PUT, and DELETE for a specific item ID.

cards.title: Group routes under an API prefix
cards.explanation: Groups the health and items routes inside a router, then mounts that router under /api so its paths become /api/health and /api/items.

cards.title: Return JSON from an Axum handler
cards.explanation: Derives serialization for a typed response and wraps it in Axum's Json so the health handler returns a JSON body containing ready: true.

cards.title: Deserialize an Axum JSON request body
cards.explanation: Deserializes an incoming JSON request body into CreateItem, prints its name, and returns HTTP 201 Created. It illustrates extraction without saving an item.

cards.title: Extract a route parameter with Axum
cards.explanation: Extracts and parses the {id} route segment as u64, then returns a text response formatted from that ID.

cards.title: Extract query parameters with Axum
cards.explanation: Deserializes URL query parameters into Page and returns its limit as text. When the optional limit is absent, the handler uses 20.

cards.title: Pass shared state to Axum handlers
cards.explanation: Stores application state in Arc, attaches it to the router, and extracts a shared reference in a handler that returns a cloned name.

cards.title: Return HTTP status codes and errors
cards.explanation: Converts a missing lookup value into an HTTP 404 response with a message. A successful lookup is returned as the handler's text response.

cards.title: Read HTTP headers with Axum
cards.explanation: Checks for the presence of an x-request-id request header and returns HTTP 200 if present or HTTP 400 if absent.

cards.title: Redirect or fall back on unknown routes
cards.explanation: Temporarily redirects GET /old to /new and supplies a text fallback for paths without a matching route.

cards.title: Wrap a handler with request middleware
cards.explanation: Logs each request's method and path, then forwards it to the next service and returns its response. The layer installs this middleware on the router.

cards.title: Stop a server on a shutdown signal
cards.explanation: Serves an Axum application until the shutdown future resolves after waiting for Ctrl+C, then performs graceful shutdown.

cards.title: Route HTTP methods with Actix Web
cards.explanation: Groups routes under /api and sends GET /api/items to list_items and POST /api/items to create_item.

cards.title: Return typed JSON with Actix Web
cards.explanation: Serializes a typed Health value through Actix Web's Json wrapper, returning a JSON response containing ready: true.

cards.title: Extract path and query parameters with Actix
cards.explanation: Extracts a numeric path parameter and query parameters into a string map, then formats both into a text response.

cards.title: Share application state with Actix Web
cards.explanation: Wraps application state in shared Data, attaches it to the app, and makes it available to a handler that returns the state's name.

cards.title: Build an Actix HTTP response
cards.explanation: Builds an HTTP 201 Created response with an x-request-id header and a JSON body indicating saved: true. The snippet constructs a response without performing storage.

cards.title: Request logging middleware with Actix
cards.code:
use actix_web::{middleware::Logger, App};

let app = App::new().wrap(Logger::default());
cards.explanation: Wraps the application with default request logging middleware. A configured logging backend is needed to display the emitted log records.

cards.title: Accept TCP connections with the standard library
cards.explanation: Binds a blocking TCP listener on localhost port 9000, accepts incoming connections, and prints each peer's address without handling its data.

cards.title: Read and write a TCP stream
cards.explanation: Connects to a TCP server, sends 'ping' followed by a newline, and reads up to 128 reply bytes. A single read may contain only part of the response.

cards.title: Send and receive UDP datagrams
cards.explanation: Receives a UDP datagram on localhost port 9001 and echoes its received bytes to the sender. UDP does not guarantee delivery or ordering.

cards.title: Accept TCP connections asynchronously with Tokio
cards.explanation: Accepts TCP connections asynchronously and starts a Tokio task for each one, moving the stream into the task for the illustrative handle() function to process.

cards.title: Async TCP reads and writes
cards.explanation: Connects and exchanges bytes asynchronously through Tokio's I/O extension traits. The read returns a byte count and may receive only part of the reply.

cards.title: Fetch an HTTP response with Reqwest
cards.explanation: Sends an asynchronous HTTP GET request, turns HTTP client or server error statuses into errors, and reads the response body as text.

cards.title: Send and receive JSON with Reqwest
cards.explanation: Sends a JSON body in an HTTP POST, checks for HTTP error statuses, and deserializes the response into a general JSON value. Reqwest's json feature is required.
